scope: Twelve original Raw slots plus Mr. Perfect. Derived from tracked evidence only; no ROM read.
claim: Complete roster animation coverage is NOT established.

art_statuses.original: Stock WWF Raw artwork, unmodified by this project
art_statuses.customized: Stock Raw body/animation with user-edited gear, head or palette
art_statuses.native_port: Donor-game drawing reproduced from native source tiles and anchors
art_statuses.adapted_placeholder: Existing Raw artwork standing in for a pose it was not drawn for
art_statuses.decoded_only: Source recipe decoded/mapped; not inserted into any shipped Raw build
art_statuses.prototype_private: Inserted only in a private test build; not released
art_statuses.missing: No suitable art exists for this role

gameplay_statuses.verified_visual: Native gameplay capture reviewed for this role and art
gameplay_statuses.verified_functional: Controller replay proves the action runs (damage/recovery); visuals not accepted
gameplay_statuses.defective: Native gameplay capture exists and shows a visible defect
gameplay_statuses.untested: No native gameplay capture for this role and art

perfect_plex_static_checks.summary: Recipe budget: worst stored record uses 17/17 objects and 52/64 tiles including the shadow (stored recipe records only; says nothing about runtime upload, scanline, routing or OAM order).
Recipe chunk order: every stored record lists 16x16 chunks before 8x8 chunks (stored recipe records only; says nothing about runtime upload, scanline, routing or OAM order).

Bounds check: with the prototype canvas shift (+9 px x) the union of chunk extents reaches every edge of each pose's opaque bbox. This does not prove every opaque pixel is covered; a union can have interior holes. The exact per-pixel check is tools/check_perfect_receiver_pixels.py (needs the Royal ROM).

Historical prototype fact: the older prototype source (and, by source inspection, the WIP builder) writes the receiver body at profile (32,0) and shadow 0x8024 at (0,-1). This check parses a copy of those bytes, not a built ROM, so it cannot detect an implementation change; a regression test must read a constructed/exported record.

One profile offset for all poses: each drawing's descriptor already carries its source-relative position, so a constant profile offset can reproduce changing body positions. Rendered positions must be derived from actor origins, profile offsets, descriptors and facing (tools/derive_perfect_pair_coordinates.py) before choosing any fix.
